comments.text: Kalimantan views the forest as an ancestor, while back home people treat it like real estate... We have so much to learn from these communities!

replies.author: @TheGlobalTruth04
replies.text: Beautifully said. ❤️ We can all learn a lot from communities that see nature as something to protect, not just something to use. Thanks for sharing your perspective! 🌿

comments.author: @RealLifeFilesDoc
comments.text: Tuning in from Vietnam! (It's 10:01 PM here). The philosophical breakdown of the Barong and Rangda dance completely changed my perspective. In Western storytelling, good always has to destroy evil, but the Balinese concept of "Rwa Bhineda"—recognizing that opposite forces must exist together to maintain cosmic balance [11:02]—is such a mature, peaceful way to look at the world. The scriptwriting captured that nuance perfectly. Thank you for making documentaries with real depth! ⚖👏

replies.author: @TheGlobalTruth04
replies.text: Thank you so much! ❤️ I'm really glad the message resonated with you. Rwa Bhineda is a beautiful philosophy, and I'm happy the documentary gave you a new perspective. Thanks for watching from Vietnam! 🇻🇳🙏
